enhanced.fullText:
The Higher Education Act Cohort Default Rate (CDR) provisions, codified at 20 U.S.C. § 1085 and implemented through 34 CFR § 668.214, establish critical institutional eligibility thresholds for participation in Title IV federal student aid programs. The CDR measures the percentage of borrowers who enter repayment on Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) or Direct Loan programs during a specific federal fiscal year and default within specified timeframes.

Under 34 CFR § 668.202, institutions face progressive sanctions based on CDR thresholds. Schools with CDRs of 30% or higher for three consecutive years lose eligibility for Direct Loan, FFEL, and Pell Grant programs. Institutions exceeding 40% in any single year face immediate loss of Direct Loan and FFEL eligibility, though Pell Grant eligibility continues under 34 CFR § 668.206.

The Department of Education calculates CDRs using data from the National Student Loan Data System (NSLDS), examining borrowers who entered repayment during the federal fiscal year two years prior to the draft calculation. For example, the FY2024 CDR examines borrowers entering repayment in FY2022. Institutions receive draft CDR data annually and may challenge calculations through data corrections or appeals under 34 CFR § 668.209.

Key statutory authority derives from 20 U.S.C. § 1015a, requiring annual CDR publication, and 20 U.S.C. § 1085, establishing eligibility standards. Recent amendments through the CARES Act temporarily excluded certain COVID-19 related forbearances from default calculations for FY2020-2023 cohorts.

Enforcement mechanisms include provisional certification under 34 CFR § 668.16, requiring increased oversight and potentially shortened certification periods. Institutions may regain eligibility by demonstrating CDR improvement below thresholds for two consecutive years or by meeting fiscal responsibility standards with enhanced monitoring.

Institutions must implement default prevention strategies, including entrance and exit counseling per 34 CFR § 685.304, and may utilize default prevention consultants to maintain compliance. The regulation applies to all Title IV-eligible institutions with borrowers entering repayment, regardless of institutional type or size.
enhanced.summary: Federal regulation establishing cohort default rate thresholds that determine institutional eligibility for Title IV programs including Direct Loans, FFEL, and Pell Grants, with sanctions for schools exceeding 30% default rates.
enhanced.requirements:
## CDR Threshold Compliance
- Maintain cohort default rates below 30% for three consecutive years to avoid program loss
- Monitor single-year rates to prevent exceeding 40% threshold triggering immediate loan program suspension
- Implement default prevention strategies per 34 CFR § 685.304

## Data Management and Monitoring
- Review annual draft CDR data from Department of Education
- Submit data corrections or appeals within 30 days of draft notification under 34 CFR § 668.209
- Maintain accurate borrower records in coordination with loan servicers

## Default Prevention Programs
- Conduct comprehensive entrance and exit counseling for all borrowers
- Establish borrower contact procedures and default aversion programs
- Consider engaging default prevention consultants for at-risk institutions

## Sanctions Response
- Develop improvement plans if CDRs approach threshold levels
- Prepare appeals documentation demonstrating exceptional mitigating circumstances
- Implement provisional certification requirements if sanctions imposed
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Annual CDR data published by Department of Education; institutions receive draft calculations for review with 30-day challenge period; final CDR publication occurs annually; no direct institutional reporting required but must maintain accurate borrower data systems.
